title: Nivat's conjecture on rectangular pattern complexity
formal: Let \(A\) be a finite nonempty alphabet and \(c:\mathbb Z^2\to A\) a configuration. If for some positive integers m,n the number \(P_c(m,n)\) of distinct m-by-n rectangular patterns occurring in c is at most mn, must c have a nonzero global period?
definitions: Put \(R_{m,n}=\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\times\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\). A pattern occurring at translation t is the function on this rectangle that sends z to c(z+t). The number of distinct such functions as \(t\in\mathbb Z^2\) varies is \(P_c(m,n)\). A nonzero global period is a vector \(h\in\mathbb Z^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}\) such that c(z+h)=c(z) for every z. Only one period is required, not two linearly independent periods.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of the stated proposition, with all its quantifiers and hypotheses. Verification of finitely many parameter values does not establish the universal assertion.
why: This connects the information in local pictures to global regularity, extending a central theorem about words to two-dimensional symbolic systems.

context_blocks.text: The June 2026 paper proves the short-rectangle case with one side four. Its statement retains arbitrary rectangles as the general conjecture.

A public repository from September 2026 claims the complete theorem and supplies Lean code. Its author explicitly notes the absence of expert mathematical digestion. This card records the claim without independently certifying the proof.
